title: Integrative Multiomics and Regulatory Network Analyses Uncovers the Role of OAS3, TRAFD1, miR-222-3p, and miR-125b-5p in Hepatitis E Virus Infection.
authors: Gupta, Sonam; Singh, Prithvi; Tasneem, Alvea; Almatroudi, Ahmad; Rahmani, Arshad Husain; Dohare, Ravins; Parveen, Shama
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学和调控网络分析鉴定HEV感染相关基因与miRNA，虽涉及转录因子TRAFD1但无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅属边缘相关。
abstract: The hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a long-ignored virus that has spread globally with time. It ranked 6th among the top risk-ranking viruses with high zoonotic spillover potential; thus, considering its viral threats is a pressing priority. The molecular pathophysiology of HEV infection or the underlying cause is limited. Therefore, we incorporated an unbiased, systematic methodology to get insights into the biological heterogeneity associated with the HEV. Our study fetched 93 and 2016 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from chronic HEV (CHEV) infection in kidney-transplant patients, followed by hub module selection from a weighted gene co-expression network (WGCN). Most of the hub genes identified in this study were associated with interferon (IFN) signaling pathways. Amongst the genes induced by IFNs, the 2'-5'-oligoadenylate synthase 3 (OAS3) protein was upregulated. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) modular, functional enrichment, and feed-forward loop (FFL) analyses led to the identification of two key miRNAs, i.e., miR-222-3p and miR-125b-5p, which showed a strong association with the OAS3 gene and TRAF-type zinc finger domain containing 1 (TRAFD1) transcription factor (TF) based on essential centrality measures. Further experimental studies are required to substantiate the significance of these FFL-associated genes and miRNAs with their respective functions in CHEV. To our knowledge, it is the first time that miR-222-3p has been described as a reference miRNA for use in CHEV sample analyses. In conclusion, our study has enlightened a few budding targets of HEV, which might help us understand the cellular and molecular pathways dysregulated in HEV through various factors. Thus, providing a novel insight into its pathophysiology and progression dynamics.
abstract_zh: 戊型肝炎病毒（HEV）是一种长期被忽视的病毒，随着时间推移已在全球范围内传播。在高人畜共患溢出潜力的风险排名病毒中，它位列第6；因此，考虑其病毒威胁是当务之急。HEV感染的分子病理生理学或其潜在病因尚不明确。因此，我们采用了一种无偏倚、系统性的方法，以深入了解与HEV相关的生物学异质性。我们的研究从肾移植患者的慢性HEV（CHEV）感染中获取了93个和2016个差异表达基因（DEGs），随后通过加权基因共表达网络（WGCN）进行核心模块选择。本研究中识别的大多数核心基因与干扰素（IFN）信号通路相关。在IFN诱导的基因中，2'-5'-寡腺苷酸合成酶3（OAS3）蛋白表达上调。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）模块分析、功能富集分析以及前馈环路（FFL）分析识别出两个关键miRNA，即miR-222-3p和miR-125b-5p，它们基于关键中心性度量与OAS3基因和含TRAF型锌指结构域1（TRAFD1）转录因子（TF）显示出强关联。需要进一步的实验研究来证实这些FFL相关基因和miRNA在CHEV中的各自功能意义。据我们所知，这是首次将miR-222-3p描述为用于CHEV样本分析的参考miRNA。总之，我们的研究揭示了HEV的一些潜在靶点，这可能有助于我们理解HEV通过多种因素失调的细胞和分子通路，从而为其病理生理学和进展动态提供新的见解。
